14.title: Advanced Waterfall: PDL, Pro-rata Sharing & Step-ups
14.prerequisite: Day 13 · Legal documents and account rules

sections.label: PDL
sections.title: A PDL records principal borrowed to protect senior interest
sections.kicker: LEDGER MODE: protect now, repay before juniors.
sections.lead: When documents permit principal to cover a senior interest shortfall, the principal deficiency ledger records the diversion and controls later payments.

bullets.title: Add
bullets.text: PDL_Add is the lesser of available principal and the permitted interest shortfall.

bullets.title: Cure
bullets.text: Cash repays the PDL in its stated priority before junior principal resumes.

bullets.title: Trap
bullets.text: Equity is typically zero while a PDL remains outstanding and tests block release.

sections.callout: A PDL delays juniors to protect senior interest; it does not erase the shortfall.

sections.label: Allocation
sections.title: Pro-rata shares principal; sequential concentrates it
sections.kicker: PAY RULE: share the pool or clear the senior class.
sections.lead: Principal allocation changes each class's paydown speed, extension risk and protection.

bullets.title: Pro-rata
bullets.text: Class share equals available principal times its beginning balance divided by all sharing classes' beginning balances.

bullets.title: Sequential
bullets.text: All principal goes to the most senior outstanding class, then the next.

bullets.title: Flip
bullets.text: OC, IC, delinquency or CNL failures can redirect pro-rata payment to sequential.

sections.callout: Pro-rata is conditional; sequential is the defensive route when protection weakens.

sections.label: Step-up
sections.title: The step-up date changes economics, not trigger authority
sections.kicker: DATE CHECK: coupon changes, document logic still wins.
sections.lead: A coupon step-up and the end of a pro-rata window can share a date, but the indenture determines their exact interaction.

bullets.title: Before
bullets.text: Many deals allow pro-rata before step-up only while all tests pass.

bullets.title: After
bullets.text: Some require hard sequential payment after step-up regardless of current trigger results.

bullets.title: Model
bullets.text: Use an After_StepUp switch to route principal through the documented rule.

sections.callout: Never infer the principal rule from the coupon change alone.

sections.label: Lab
sections.title: Trace add, cure and allocation across three months
sections.kicker: SIMULATION: shortfall first, cure next, sharing last.
sections.lead: Build an auditable path that explains every change in cash direction.

bullets.title: Month 1
bullets.text: Use 30k principal for a 30k interest shortfall, record PDL_Add, then pay remaining principal sequentially.

bullets.title: Month 2
bullets.text: Use positive excess spread to cure the 30k PDL and show whether equity remains off or resumes.

bullets.title: Month 3
bullets.text: With tests passing before step-up, allocate principal pro-rata by A and B beginning balances.

sections.callout: Report PDL Beg/Add/Cure/End, A/B principal, equity status and the flip date.

flashcards.back: A ledger of principal used for permitted interest shortfalls, generally cured before junior principal resumes.
Principal shared by each participating class's beginning-balance proportion.
Principal paid to the most senior outstanding class before moving down the stack.
A model switch applying the documented allocation rule after the coupon step-up date.
A trigger failure or date rule that changes principal payment from pro-rata to sequential.

options: Principal used for permitted interest shortfalls
quiz.explain: It records principal diverted to cover a permitted interest shortfall.

quiz.q: Where is PDL cure generally placed?
quiz.explain: Cure restores diverted principal before juniors resume paydown.
Each sharing class receives its proportion of total beginning balances.

quiz.q: What typically happens while PDL is outstanding?
quiz.explain: Residual cash is generally blocked until cure and passing tests.
OC/IC, delinquency/CNL or documented step-up conditions can flip allocation.

sections.label: Roles
sections.title: Each counterparty controls a different operational risk
sections.kicker: TEAM MAP: collect, hold, calculate, hedge.
sections.lead: The deal depends on parties that move cash, apply the waterfall, safeguard accounts and manage rate exposure.

bullets.title: Servicing
bullets.text: The servicer collects cash; backup readiness determines transition risk after a trigger.

bullets.title: Trustee
bullets.text: The trustee calculates tests, runs the waterfall, pays notes and enforces mechanics.

bullets.title: Bank and hedge
bullets.text: The account bank holds trust cash; a swap or cap provider manages rate mismatch when present.

sections.callout: Healthy collateral cannot compensate for an operational break in the cash chain.

sections.label: Cash control
sections.title: Lockboxes and sweeps reduce commingling exposure
sections.kicker: CASH PATH: shorten the distance to protected accounts.
sections.lead: Controls limit how long borrower collections remain exposed to the servicer or an ineligible bank.

bullets.title: Lockbox
bullets.text: Collections enter a blocked account instead of remaining freely available to the servicer.

bullets.title: Sweeps
bullets.text: Daily or weekly sweeps move cash to P&I and reserve accounts.

bullets.title: Permitted investments
bullets.text: Ratings and tenor limits constrain temporary investment of trust cash.

sections.callout: Shorter remittance periods reduce commingling without changing borrower performance.

sections.label: Downgrade
sections.title: Eligibility breaches activate a remedy menu
sections.kicker: RATING DROP: replace, support, collateralize or exit.
sections.lead: Minimum ratings determine who can hold trust cash or owe the trust money.

bullets.title: Replace
bullets.text: Move the role to an eligible substitute within the stated deadline.

bullets.title: Support
bullets.text: Use an eligible guarantor or post cash or collateral under a CSA.

bullets.title: Swap remedy
bullets.text: Novate to an eligible bank or terminate at market under the ISDA schedule.

sections.callout: Ordering and deadlines are deal-specific and monitored by the trustee.

sections.label: Scenario
sections.title: Choose the remedy when ratings fall
sections.kicker: CONTROL ROOM: preserve cash and hedge continuity.
sections.lead: Map each breach to its operational response and daily cash consequence.

bullets.title: Servicer
bullets.text: On a threshold breach, spring the lockbox and move to daily sweeps; optional advances may stop and thin IC.

bullets.title: Account bank
bullets.text: Replace within 30 days or add an eligible guaranty while using only overnight eligible investments.

bullets.title: Swap provider
bullets.text: At BBB+, require CSA collateral; after a further downgrade, novate or terminate at market.

sections.callout: For each party, record the eligibility test, deadline, remedy and cash-handling change.

flashcards.back: Exposure while borrower collections remain with the servicer before reaching trust accounts.
A party meeting documented minimum ratings and other criteria for its role.
Tighter cash control activated after a specified downgrade or trigger.
A credit support annex governing collateral for derivative exposure.
A designated party prepared at a hot or cold level to take over servicing.

quiz.explain: Controlled accounts and faster sweeps reduce servicer-held cash.

quiz.q: What can follow an account-bank eligibility breach?
options: Move accounts to an eligible bank
quiz.explain: Replacement or eligible support protects trust cash.

quiz.q: Where do regular hedge costs usually sit?
quiz.explain: They are commonly senior, subject to exact priority.
Collateral can be faster than immediate novation and covers current exposure.

quiz.q: Why can optional advances weaken IC?
options: Interest may not be fronted in stress
quiz.explain: Collections may then be insufficient for senior interest and fees.

16.title: Static Pool & Vintage Analysis; Roll-Rates Lab
16.later: Day 17 · Data tape and collateral stratification

sections.label: Vintage
sections.title: A static pool compares like loans at the same age
sections.kicker: COHORT VIEW: hold the starting group still.
sections.lead: Track loans originated together by months since origination so changing pool composition does not obscure performance.

bullets.title: Cohort
bullets.text: Keep the original group fixed for comparable timing.

bullets.title: CNL
bullets.text: Cumulative net losses through month t divided by original cohort balance.

bullets.title: Seasoning
bullets.text: Delinquencies often rise early and later flatten as surviving borrowers build equity.

sections.callout: The fixed cohort makes loss timing comparable across origination periods.

sections.label: Two views
sections.title: Vintage and trust views answer different questions
sections.kicker: TWO LENSES: assumptions versus actual deal cash.
sections.lead: Vintage data calibrates expected behavior; trust data shows trigger and cash outcomes for the securitized pool.

bullets.title: Vintage
bullets.text: Compare prime/subprime, period, dealer or geography cohorts.

bullets.title: Trust
bullets.text: Observe the actual pool after prepayment and collateral cut-off effects.

bullets.title: Normalize
bullets.text: State whether every ratio uses original or current balance.

sections.callout: Use vintage to choose assumptions and trust performance to test the deal.

sections.label: Roll-rates
sections.title: Transitions show where delinquent loans are going
sections.kicker: PIPELINE: Current → 30 → 60 → 90 → charge-off.
sections.lead: Roll-rates measure migration between delinquency states and help estimate loss timing.

bullets.text: Current 60-day balance divided by prior-month 30-day balance, with normalization stated.

bullets.title: Late stage
bullets.text: Rising 60→90 and 90→CO signal near-term charge-off pressure.

bullets.title: Recovery lag
bullets.text: Apply recoveries after charge-offs to reflect repossession and auction timing.

sections.callout: A transition matrix shows direction, not only today's stock of delinquency.

sections.label: Lab
sections.title: Compare two cohorts and redesign protection
sections.kicker: ANALYST LAB: calculate, stress, decide.
sections.lead: Build six-month prime and subprime vintages, then turn their behavior into structural judgment.

bullets.title: Calculate
bullets.text: Compute 30→60, 60→90, 90→CO and month-6 CNL for each cohort.

bullets.title: Stress
bullets.text: Raise severity 10 points with defaults unchanged and recalculate net loss and CNL.

bullets.title: Decide
bullets.text: Name the cohort needing thicker CE and propose 60+ and CNL thresholds that flip it sequential.

sections.callout: Faster rolls and higher severity compress XS, slow OC build and delay equity.

flashcards.back: A fixed cohort tracked by months since origination.
Cumulative net losses divided by original cohort balance.
The share moving from one delinquency state to the next.
The transition from 90-day delinquency to charge-off.
How performance changes as a loan cohort ages.

options: Compare like loans at the same age
quiz.explain: A fixed cohort provides comparable loss timing.
The original cohort is the denominator.

quiz.q: Which roll is closest to charge-off?
quiz.explain: It is the last transition before realized loss.

quiz.q: Higher severity with equal defaults does what?
quiz.explain: Lower recoveries raise net loss.

quiz.q: How should faster rolls affect structure?
quiz.explain: Faster deterioration requires greater protection and earlier action.

17.title: Data Tape & Collateral Stratification
17.shortTitle: Turn loan rows into risk signals
17.later: Day 18 · Investor memo and credit pitch

sections.label: Tape
sections.title: The loan-level tape is the raw material for collateral analysis
sections.kicker: DATA INVENTORY: borrower, vehicle, payment, place.
sections.lead: Connect contract terms, borrower risk, vehicle attributes, payment history and concentrations for each loan.

bullets.title: Contract
bullets.text: ID, dates, balances, APR, term and remaining term.

bullets.title: Borrower and vehicle
bullets.text: FICO or score, income ratios, new/used, make, model, year and LTV.

bullets.title: Behavior and place
bullets.text: Delinquency, extensions, state, dealer and channel where available.

sections.callout: A strat is reliable only when field definitions are clear.

sections.label: Hygiene
sections.title: Validate before you aggregate
sections.kicker: QUALITY GATE: catch false risk signals.
sections.lead: Simple checks prevent conclusions based on duplicates, missing values or impossible ranges.

bullets.title: Keys
bullets.text: Flag duplicate or missing IDs and negative balances.

bullets.title: Ranges
bullets.text: Review dates, APR, term, LTV outliers and zero values.

bullets.title: Deferrals
bullets.text: Count extensions because high use can postpone visible delinquency.

sections.callout: Identify and explain outliers rather than silently deleting them.

sections.label: Strats
sections.title: A compact strat pack reveals the pool's shape
sections.kicker: SLICE MODE: measure the center and tails.
sections.lead: Balance-weighted distributions show where risk clusters beyond a single average.

bullets.title: Credit and term
bullets.text: Show FICO bands, term buckets and weighted-average remaining term.

bullets.title: LTV and vehicle
bullets.text: Show LTV buckets, tail shares, WA LTV and new/used mix.

bullets.title: Concentration
bullets.text: Report top states and top dealers by pool share.

sections.callout: A safe-looking average can hide a material risky tail.

sections.label: Challenge
sections.title: Turn a weak mix into structural asks
sections.kicker: CREDIT CHALLENGE: diagnose, protect, monitor.
sections.lead: Given Used 65%, LTV above 120% at 12%, FICO below 620 at 20% and term 73+ at 18%, recommend action.

bullets.title: Risk
bullets.text: High LTV and used share raise severity; low scores and long terms raise loss and extension risk.

bullets.title: Structure
bullets.text: Ask for a higher OC target and tighter 60+/CNL flip conditions with a shorter pro-rata window.

bullets.title: Surveillance
bullets.text: Track extensions and late-stage roll-rates as forbearance ends.

sections.callout: State which tail drives each recommendation so the ask remains auditable.

flashcards.back: Loan-level contract, borrower, vehicle, performance and concentration data.
The balance-weighted average loan-to-value ratio.
Pool percentage beyond a chosen risk threshold.
A payment accommodation that can postpone visible delinquency.
Pool exposure tied to one dealer or a small group.

quiz.q: Which trio supports a first-pass strat?
quiz.explain: They are core loan-level risk fields.
Vehicle value and borrower equity drive recoveries.

quiz.q: Why do long terms extend senior risk?
quiz.explain: Seniors can remain outstanding longer.

quiz.q: What does a high-LTV tail imply?
quiz.explain: Less borrower equity weakens recovery.

quiz.q: How should a weak mix affect pro-rata?
quiz.explain: Tighter conditions protect seniors.

18.title: Investor Memo & Credit Committee Pitch
18.prerequisite: Day 17 · Data tape and collateral stratification
18.later: Day 19 · Regulation, disclosure and risk retention

sections.label: Memo
sections.title: A one-page memo connects collateral, structure and pricing
sections.kicker: EXECUTIVE VIEW: evidence, judgment, action.
sections.lead: Let a decision-maker understand the deal and recommendation without rebuilding the analysis.

bullets.title: Snapshot
bullets.text: Issuer, series, FICO, used share, WA APR, term, LTV and concentrations.

bullets.title: Structure
bullets.text: Classes, ratings, OC, reserve, pay rules, PDL and triggers.

bullets.title: Decision
bullets.text: Base/stress results, risks, mitigants, pricing and monitoring.

sections.callout: Explain why facts support the recommendation; do not merely list them.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.title: Every conclusion should trace to a source
sections.kicker: PROOF CHAIN: presale + tape + model.
sections.lead: Use complementary evidence so the pitch remains auditable.

bullets.title: Presale
bullets.text: Base loss, severity, rating stresses, reserve and trigger curves.

bullets.title: Tape
bullets.text: Low-FICO, high-LTV, long-term, used and concentration tails.

bullets.title: Model
bullets.text: OC cure, equity trap, senior WAL and PDL path.

sections.callout: Connect each material risk to a mitigant that can actually absorb it.

sections.label: Pricing
sections.title: Use WAL-matched comps and explain every deviation
sections.kicker: RELATIVE VALUE: compare like risk and timing.
sections.lead: Illustrative ranges become useful only when the memo explains why this deal should price tighter or wider.

bullets.title: Senior
bullets.text: The note illustrates T+100–120 bps for AAA around 2.5–3.0y WAL with tight structure.

bullets.title: Mezz
bullets.text: It illustrates T+200–350 bps for A/BBB around 1.5–2.5y WAL, depending on CE and context.

bullets.title: Difference
bullets.text: Weak tails or long pro-rata widen; daily sweeps, strict flips and fast cure can tighten.

sections.callout: The framework matters more than the illustrative spread range.

sections.label: Pitch
sections.title: Defend a concrete recommendation under Q&A
sections.kicker: COMMITTEE SIMULATION: answer the question behind the question.
sections.lead: Pitch the source note's example and make the timeline decision-ready.

bullets.title: Recommendation
bullets.text: Heavy used and high-LTV tails are offset by 12% OC and strict 60+/CNL flips.

bullets.title: Stress path
bullets.text: Equity is off P1–P2, OC cures by P3 and senior WAL holds near 2.7 years.

bullets.title: Price and monitor
bullets.text: Defend T+112 senior and T+270 mezz talk; flag 60+ above 2.25% or OC below 1.10x.

sections.callout: Prepare concise answers on the worst tail, sequential flip, cure speed and servicer downgrade response.

flashcards.back: A decision document connecting collateral, structure, model, risk, pricing and monitoring.
A comparable bond with similar weighted-average life.
The period when OC returns to target under a scenario.
How long residual cash remains blocked.
A KPI level that triggers review or assumption changes.

quiz.explain: FICO and LTV describe receivables.
Riskier collateral and weaker protection demand spread.

options: How quickly triggers force sequential pay
quiz.explain: Defensive principal routing controls senior paydown.
Late delinquency migration approaches realized loss.
They show protection and extension behavior.

19.title: Regulation, Disclosure & Risk Retention
19.prerequisite: Day 18 · Investor memo and credit pitch
19.later: Day 20 · Macro drivers and scenario design

sections.label: Pathways
sections.title: Public and 144A deals expose information differently
sections.kicker: ROUTE CHECK: identify the issuance path first.
sections.lead: The route determines formal disclosure and where ongoing reports live.

bullets.title: Public
bullets.text: SEC-registered deals follow Reg AB II and recurring filings.

bullets.title: 144A
bullets.text: Private QIB deals use an OM and trustee or servicer packages rather than an SEC shelf and 10-D.

bullets.title: Sources
bullets.text: Use EDGAR for public filings and trustee, issuer or agency portals for other reports.

sections.callout: Presale analysis may exist under either pathway.

sections.label: Transparency
sections.title: Reg AB II and Rule 17g-5 solve different problems
sections.kicker: DISCLOSURE MAP: investor reporting versus rating access.
sections.lead: One standardizes public ABS disclosure; the other supports equal access to rating information.

bullets.title: Reg AB II
bullets.text: Covers collateral, structure, risks, servicing and static pools where applicable.

bullets.title: Forms
bullets.text: 10-D is monthly, 10-K annual and 8-K reports material events.

bullets.title: 17g-5
bullets.text: An arranger site shares rating exchanges with hired and non-hired NRSROs where applicable.

sections.callout: Rule 17g-5 is intended to reduce ratings shopping.

sections.label: Retention
sections.title: The 5% rule can be vertical, horizontal or L-shaped
sections.kicker: ALIGNMENT: retain exposure to what you create.
sections.lead: Retention form determines which layer the sponsor or eligible affiliate continues to bear.

bullets.title: Vertical
bullets.text: Retain 5% of each tranche.

bullets.title: Horizontal
bullets.text: Retain a 5% fair-value first-loss or equity interest.

bullets.title: L-shaped
bullets.text: Combine vertical and horizontal pieces to meet the requirement.

sections.callout: Verify the holder, sizing basis and deal-specific hold period in the documents.

sections.label: Diligence
sections.title: Compare a public deal with a 144A deal
sections.kicker: COMPLIANCE LAB: path, reports, retention, jurisdiction.
sections.lead: Build a source map for Auto 2025-A 144A and Prime Auto 2025-A public.

bullets.title: Reporting
bullets.text: For each, identify the trustee portal or EDGAR forms and likely asset-level/static-pool disclosure.

bullets.title: Retention
bullets.text: Name the holder and choose vertical, horizontal or L-shaped, explaining the economic alignment.

bullets.title: EU/UK
bullets.text: If relevant, record 5% retention, ESMA templates, due diligence and any STS status.

sections.callout: STS means Simple, Transparent and Standardised and can affect investor comfort or capital treatment.

flashcards.back: The US public ABS disclosure framework.
A private offering route to qualified institutional buyers.
A rating-information access rule intended to reduce ratings shopping.
Retention of the required first-loss or equity interest.
Simple, Transparent and Standardised under the EU framework.

quiz.q: Which forms recur for public ABS?
quiz.explain: 10-D is monthly and 10-K annual; 8-K covers material events.
Vertical, horizontal and L-shaped are described.
It promotes equal rating-information access.
Private reporting is commonly hosted by trustee or issuer.
It is the EU designation named in the note.

20.title: Macro Drivers & Scenario Design
20.shortTitle: Translate the economy into deal stress
20.prerequisite: Day 19 · Regulation, disclosure and risk retention

sections.label: Drivers
sections.title: Macro variables reach ABS through borrowers and vehicles
sections.kicker: CAUSE MAP: jobs, prices, rates, costs, supply.
sections.lead: Each series matters because it changes payment capacity, recovery value, prepayment or expenses.

bullets.title: Labor
bullets.text: Unemployment and claims affect delinquencies and defaults.

bullets.title: Vehicles
bullets.text: Used-car auction values drive recovery severity.

bullets.title: Rates and costs
bullets.text: Rates affect affordability and prepay; inflation and fuel squeeze budgets and fees.

sections.callout: Always explain the path from the economy to deal cash.

sections.label: Inputs
sections.title: Convert the narrative into parameters
sections.kicker: TRANSLATOR: story → rolls, severity, prepay, fees.
sections.lead: A scenario becomes testable when each claim changes a specific input for a stated duration.

bullets.title: Labor shock
bullets.text: Raise 60+/90+ rolls and charge-offs with a lag.

bullets.title: Price shock
bullets.text: Lower recoveries and raise severity while keeping defaults separately visible.

bullets.title: Rate/cost shock
bullets.text: Slow prepay, extend WAL and raise fees that compress XS.

sections.callout: Do not stress CNL as a black box when frequency, severity and timing can be separated.

sections.label: Dashboard
sections.title: Thresholds turn monitoring into action
sections.kicker: CONTROL PANEL: green, amber, red—and act.
sections.lead: Combine deal KPIs and macro feeds with responses aligned to trigger logic.

bullets.title: KPIs
bullets.text: Track 60+, 90+, severity, recoveries, OC, XS, principal and PDL.

bullets.title: Feeds
bullets.text: Watch claims, used-car index, CPI and 2y/3y Treasury yields.

bullets.title: Action
bullets.text: Tighten on amber; on red, model trapped equity and hard sequential pay until cure.

sections.callout: A status light without an action is decoration.

sections.label: Scenario
sections.title: Run a severe three-period macro path
sections.kicker: STRESS LAB: map, run, decide.
sections.lead: Model used-car prices down 12%, unemployment up 1 point and rates up 75 bps.

bullets.title: Inputs
bullets.text: Raise severity 10 points and late roll-rates, cut prepay 15%, and add 7k monthly fees.

bullets.title: Outputs
bullets.text: OC fails P1-P2 and cures P3; A WAL extends 2.6y to 2.9y; equity stays off until P3.

bullets.title: Decision
bullets.text: Widen talk 20–30 bps and define actions at 60+ amber 2.25% and red 2.75%.

sections.callout: Record magnitude, duration, cash outcome and action for both mild and severe cases.

flashcards.back: A factor such as used-car prices that changes recovery for the same defaults.
Turning an economic story into explicit model inputs.
An increase in weighted-average life from slower paydown.
A threshold and duration rule linked to a cash action.
An early-warning level prompting tighter assumptions or review.

quiz.explain: Vehicle values determine recovery proceeds.

quiz.q: How does unemployment enter the model?
quiz.explain: Payment stress first raises delinquency migration.
Slower refinancing keeps notes outstanding.
They measure performance and protection.

quiz.q: Which is a full scenario mapping?
options: Jobs +1 point, cars -8%, rolls +50 bps, severity +8, prepay -10%
quiz.explain: It converts the story into measurable inputs.

21.title: Servicing, Repossession & Recoveries
21.prerequisite: Day 20 · Macro drivers and scenario design
21.later: Day 22 · Deal lifecycle and post-close surveillance

sections.label: Lifecycle
sections.title: Default management is a sequence
sections.kicker: OPERATIONS FLOW: miss → cure → repo → sale → deficiency.
sections.lead: Servicing policy determines how a missed payment reaches charge-off and recovery.

bullets.title: Cure
bullets.text: Loans move through 30/60/90 while outreach continues.

bullets.title: Repo and sale
bullets.text: After charge-off, the vehicle is secured, prepared and sold net of costs.

bullets.title: Deficiency
bullets.text: Unpaid balance remains after sale; later collection is often low.

sections.callout: The operating path controls when loss and recovery cash appear.

sections.label: Timing
sections.title: Cures, auction lags and advances reshape cash
sections.kicker: CLOCK RISK: the same loss can arrive differently.
sections.lead: Timing changes delinquency visibility, IC and the period in which losses pressure OC.

bullets.title: Cure window
bullets.text: Faster cures reduce loss migration; long queues increase 60+/90+.

bullets.title: Auction lag
bullets.text: Delay from charge-off to proceeds shifts recovery timing.

bullets.title: Support
bullets.text: Deferrals postpone stress; optional advances can thin IC when collections fall.

sections.callout: A temporary delinquency improvement may reflect timing support, not stronger borrowers.

sections.label: Severity
sections.title: Recovery depends on vehicle, leverage, cost and channel
sections.kicker: RECOVERY MATH: sale proceeds minus friction.
sections.lead: Severity rises when collateral sells for less or the process consumes more proceeds.

bullets.title: Vehicle
bullets.text: Index, make, model, year, mileage and condition drive gross value.

bullets.title: LTV
bullets.text: Higher current LTV means less borrower equity and weaker balance recovery.

bullets.title: Costs/channel
bullets.text: Repo, storage, transport, legal, auction, reconditioning and sale route affect net cash.

sections.callout: Severity is the loss after recovery economics, not merely default occurrence.

sections.label: Lab
sections.title: Stress two months of recovery performance
sections.kicker: CASH-FLOW LAB: charge off, recover, redirect.
sections.lead: Use the provided gross charge-off and recovery paths to see how severity reaches the waterfall.

bullets.title: Month 1
bullets.text: GCO 400k less 180k recoveries gives 220k net loss; calculate severity and XS effect.

bullets.title: Month 2
bullets.text: GCO 450k less 150k recoveries gives 300k net loss; retest IC, OC and equity status.

bullets.title: Decision
bullets.text: Explain whether to trap XS, turbo seniors, flip sequential or accrue PDL, and add one severity dashboard alert.

sections.callout: The note's separate example, 400k charge-offs less 170k recovery, implies 57.5% severity.

flashcards.back: Amount unpaid after vehicle sale and other recoveries.
Delay between charge-off or repossession and sale proceeds.
Net loss relative to gross charge-offs in the simplified measure.
Interest support a servicer may decline to make in stress.
Sale proceeds after repo, storage, transport, legal and auction costs.

options: Repo, storage, transport and auction costs
quiz.explain: Operating and sale costs reduce proceeds.

options: Delay delinquency and cluster later losses
quiz.explain: They postpone rather than necessarily remove stress.

quiz.q: Why do optional advances raise IC risk?
quiz.explain: Senior interest then relies on weaker current collections.
Auction values track the used-vehicle market.

options: Trap XS and turbo or sequential pay
quiz.explain: Loss pressure activates structural defenses.

22.title: Deal Lifecycle: Warehouse to Term ABS & Post-Close
22.shortTitle: Follow the deal from ramp to surveillance
22.later: Day 23 · Relative value and comparable deals

sections.label: Warehouse
sections.title: The warehouse finances receivables before term take-out
sections.kicker: LIFECYCLE START: originate, qualify, finance, select.
sections.lead: A lender advances against eligible receivables until a selected pool moves to the SPV and term notes repay the warehouse.

bullets.title: Facility
bullets.text: Eligibility and advance rates govern warehouse funding.

bullets.title: Triggers
bullets.text: Warehouse amortization tests protect the lender and differ from term ABS tests.

bullets.title: Take-out
bullets.text: True sale transfers the pool; note proceeds repay warehouse funding.

sections.callout: Term collateral is already shaped by warehouse rules.

sections.label: Ramp
sections.title: Prefunding and substitution add controlled flexibility
sections.kicker: CONTROLLED CHANGE: add or replace within the rules.
sections.lead: Post-close collateral changes are limited by amount, time, eligibility and oversight.

bullets.title: Prefunding
bullets.text: Add a capped amount of eligible collateral during a short window through a prefunding account.

bullets.title: Substitution
bullets.text: Replace or repurchase an ineligible or representation-breach asset under the PSA.

bullets.title: Oversight
bullets.text: Trustee approval or notice and reporting make every addition auditable.

sections.callout: Prefunding is a controlled ramp, not open permission to change the pool.

sections.label: Closing
sections.title: Closing aligns documents, ratings, accounts and settlement
sections.kicker: LAUNCH CHECKLIST: every dependency ready.
sections.lead: Legal transfer, account funding, pricing, DTC settlement and reporting must coordinate.

bullets.title: Documents
bullets.text: Finalize indenture, PSA, account agreement, offering materials and legal opinions.

bullets.title: Funding
bullets.text: Fund reserve and prefunding accounts and settle notes through DTC.

bullets.title: Operations
bullets.text: Finalize ratings and pricing, release cash, set payment dates and load trustee templates.

sections.callout: The closing checklist links legal validity to the first payment cycle.

sections.label: Simulation
sections.title: Run the first 90 days and prepare for the tail
sections.kicker: POST-CLOSE LAB: reconcile, monitor, communicate.
sections.lead: Test the example deal with 12% OC, 1.5% reserve and 5% prefunding due in 30 days.

bullets.title: Month 1
bullets.text: Reconcile the trustee waterfall at OC 1.11x and 60+ at 1.2%; confirm modest equity is permitted.

bullets.title: Month 2
bullets.text: Verify prefunding completed under the same eligibility and log any substitution or repurchase.

bullets.title: Escalate and exit
bullets.text: Define review triggers for 60+/90+, severity, OC, reserve or PDL, and note the optional clean-up around 10% of original collateral.

sections.callout: Material breaches, counterparty changes and amendments require investor communication.

flashcards.back: Financing for eligible receivables before term ABS take-out.
A capped, time-limited addition of eligible collateral after close.
Replacing an ineligible or representation-breach asset under the PSA.
Term ABS issuance that repays warehouse funding.
Optional redemption when collateral falls below a documented original-balance threshold.

quiz.explain: It bridges origination to term take-out.
It is constrained by window, amount, eligibility and oversight.

quiz.q: What should be verified early with the trustee?
quiz.explain: Early surveillance confirms the deal operates as designed.
